text:
Alex: Quick sync — proposing a short, repeatable protocol for apples-to-apples kernel + batching comparisons. We need one unambiguous recipe so synthetic vs replay runs are comparable.
Priya: +1. can you sketch the steps?
Alex: High level: 1) fixed traffic profile (seq len dist + prompt mix), 2) single-model weight (no quant diff), 3) run replay harness and synthetic generator with same interarrival and burst parameters, 4) collect TTFT, TPOT, p95/p99, goodput, and kernel-level counters.
Jon: How do you want to normalize the seq len distribution between replay and synth? replay is messy.
Alex: Use deterministic bucketing: compute empirical seq len histogram from replay trace, then feed the synthetic generator to sample from that histogram. That keeps distribution identical.
Marta: We should pin RNG seeds and sticky session mapping so KV cache warms deterministically for replay-vs-synth comparisons.
Ethan: Important: warm KV cache vs cold-start runs are different stories. For apples-to-apples include both phases but label them. Otherwise TTFT p95 will be dominated by cold miss noise.
Priya: Agree. Proposed run set: (A) cold-start ramp (5m), (B) warmed steady-state (20m), (C) overload/backpressure sweep. All runs with same batching heuristic config.
Alex: Batching heuristics: run with both 'adaptive' and 'static' modes. Note: adaptive's internal timers can interact with arrival jitter; include high-jitter synthetic shots to test fragility.
Jon: For kernel selection vs quantization tests: keep same runtime path except kernel variant. In practice we toggle kernel selector flag and restart. Capture kernel name and variant in metrics.
Marta: Data to capture per request: model_variant, kernel_name, batch_size, trace_id, kv_hit_ratio, request_seq_len, response_token_count, latency_server_side (TTFT), p50/p95/p99, tokens_emitted. Also counters: kernel_time, decode_time, queuing_time.
Ethan: Definitions so we're consistent: TTFT = time from request received at runtime ingress to first token emitted by runtime to client. TPOT = total time to produce N output tokens (use 50 tokens as canonical for p95 reporting), goodput = successful output tokens / wall time excluding retries. QPS alone is misleading because varying token lengths change work per request.
Priya: Where do we compute queuing vs kernel exec? add micro-profiling: grpc handler entry -> enqueue -> batch pop -> kernel exec -> postprocess. We have timestamps for each.
Alex: Yes, include those spans. Benchbot: automated note: run template saved as bench/apples_to_apples_v1.json.
Jon: For statistical rigor, run each config 5x on separate hosts (or different gpu pools) and compute median + bootstrapped 95% CI for p95.
Marta: Also collect per-kernel percent of batches with size < target, since batching efficiency matters.
Ethan: Regression detection: keep a baseline artifact of kernel-level counters and TTFT distribution. New runs diffed vs baseline; raise alert if median TTFT increases >5% or p95 increases >10% or goodput drops >4%.
Priya: Reporting: single CSV per run + JSON summary with counters and config. Add a small md report with plots: ttft_cdf, tpots_by_variant, kernel_time_stack.
Alex: Example synthetic config snippet to lock arrival jitter and seed:
```json
{
  "seed": 42,
  "arrival_jitter_ms": 12,
  "profile_histogram": "profiles/2026-01-14-frontend-hist.json",
  "session_kv_warm_fraction": 0.6
}
```
Marta: One more: include an 'equivalence check' that fails the run if the sampled seq-len histogram KL divergence between replay and synth > 0.01. Keeps us honest.
Jon: Nice. Do we need special infra to pin kernel selection to avoid other runtime heuristics changing?
Alex: We'll set an env var runtime.KERNEL_SELECTOR=explicit and read kernel_map from experiment config. Restart runtime to apply. Record the binary git SHA too.
Priya: OK I'll draft the bench template and shove to bench/recipes. Can we schedule a first comparison job Monday?
Ethan: I'll reserve GPUs and seed the replay trace.
Benchbot: job queued: apples-compare-1710043200 (ETA Monday). :robot_face: 
Alex: Great — after the first run we'll reconvene and iterate on any missing counters. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
